questions.question: What price (in Rs.) should Radha mark on a bag which costs Rs. 1680 so as to earn a profit of 25% after allowing a discount of 16% on the marked price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price is Rs. 1680.

Desired profit to earn is 25%

Discount given is 16%

**Concept Used:**

S.P = C.P + Profit

S.P = M.P - Discount

Calculation:

S.P of the bag = 1680 + 1680 × 1/4

⇒ 1680 + 420

⇒ 2100

Let the Marked Price (M.P) of the bag be Rs. M.

According to the question,

M - M × 16% = 2100

⇒ M - M × 0.16 = 2100

⇒ M (1 - 0.16) = 2100

⇒ M × 0.84 = 2100

⇒ M = 2500

So, MP = Rs. 2500

∴ Radha should mark the bag as Rs. 2500.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/661340121ece4245dffae37dda41ddab0ce1f2bf0ba4a0210bff82185deedb2e.png] __Shortcut Trick__Let the marked price of the bag be A.

According to the question,

A × 0.84 = 1680 × 1.25

⇒ A = 2500

∴ Radha should mark the bag as Rs. 2500.

Let Cosθ be P

2 P²- 5 P + 2 = 0

questions.question: If (x)/(y)+(y)/(x)=2 (x, y ≠ 0), then the value of (x - y) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

**(x)/(y)+(y)/(x)=2**

**Concept used:**

(x - y)² = (x2 - 2xy + y2)

**Calculation:**

x/y + y/x = 2

⇒ {(x × x) + (y × y)}/(x × y) = 2

⇒ (x² + y²)/xy = 2

⇒ (x2 + y2) = 2xy ----(1)

Now,

(x - y)

⇒ √(x - y)²

⇒ √(x2 - 2xy + y2)

⇒ √(x2 + y2 - 2xy)

⇒ √(2xy - 2xy) (From (1))

⇒ 0

**∴ The required value of (x - y) is 0.**

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 10 hours and 16 hours respectively. They are opened alternately for 1 hour each, opening pipe B first, in how many hours, will the empty tank be filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A fills the empty tank in 10 hours

Pipe B fills the empty tank in 16 hours

**Concept Used:**

Total work = LCM of time taken by each pipe

**Calculation:**

LCM of 16 and 10 = 80

Let total work be 80 units

Pipe A does = 80/10 = 8 units per hour

Pipe B does = 80/16 = 5 units per hour

Now,

Pipe B & A fill the tank in two hour

⇒ (5 + 8) units

⇒ 13 units

Now,

Each B & A will keep filling the tank for = (80/13) ≈ 6 hours 

After (6 × 2) = 12 hours, the tank will be filled by (13 × 6) = 78 units. 

2 units are yet to be filled

On, 13th hour B will be opened. 

It will take 2/5 hour for B to fill the remaining tank entirely.

Total time = 12 + 2/5 = 12(2)/(5) hours 

**∴ The empty tank will be filled in 12(2)/(5) hours.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold two items. The selling price of the first item equals the cost price of the second item. He sold the first item at a profit of 20% and the second item at a loss of 10%, What is his overall profit loss percent?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit on 1st item = 20%

Loss on second item = 10%

**Concept Used:**

S.P = C.P × (1 + profit percentage)

S.P = C.P × (1 - loss percentage)

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price (C.P) of the first item be Rs. 100x.

Now,

S.P of the first item = 100x × 1.2 = Rs. 120x

C.P of the second item = Rs. 120x

S.P of the second item = 120x × 0.9 = Rs. 108x

C.P of both items = (100x + 120x) = Rs. 220x

S.P of both items = (120x + 108x) = Rs. 228x

Overall profit at the end of both transaction = (228x - 220x) = Rs. 8x

Profit percentage = (8x/220x) × 100% = 3(7)/(11)%

**∴ The overall profit percentage is 3(7)/(11)%**

questions.question: What is the sum of the digits of the largest five digit number which is divisible by 5, 35, 39 and 65?
questions.solution:
Given:

Numbers are 5, 35, 39 and 65

Concept used:

The smallest number that is divisible by a series of numbers is their LCM.

Calculation:

LCM (5, 35, 39, 65) = 1365

Largest five-digit number = 99999

The approximate quotient when 99999 is divided by 1365

⇒ 99999 ÷ 1365 ≈ 73

The largest five-digit number which is divisible by 1365

⇒ 73 × 1365

⇒ 99645

So, the largest five-digit number which is divisible by 5, 35, 39 & 65 is 99645

Now,

The sum of digits of 99645 = 9 + 9 + 6 + 4 + 5 = 33

**∴ The sum of the digits of the largest five digit number which is divisible by 5, 35, 39 and 65 is 33.**

The present population of a village is 15280. If the number of males increase by 25% and the number of females increase by 15%, then the population will become 18428. The difference between present population of males and females in the village is:
questions.solution:
**Given:** 

The present population of the village is 15280

Male population increases by 25% i.e. 1/4

Female population increases by 15% i.e. 3/20

Population become after increment 18428

**Concept used:**

The Elimination Method for solving linear equations

**Calculation:**

Let the present male & female population be M & F respectively.

According to the question,

M + F = 15280 ....(1)

Then,

After increment male population = M + M × 1/4 = 5M/4

After increment Female population = F + F × 3/20 = 23F/20

According to the question,

(5M/4) + (23F/20) = 18428 ....(2)

Now, solving (1) & (2), we get M = 8560 & F = 6720.

Now, the difference between the present male & female population = M - F = 8560 - 6720 = 1840.

**∴ The difference between the present population of males and females in the village is 1840.**

questions.question: The ratio of monthly incomes of A and B is 4 ∶ 5 and that of their monthly expenditures is 3 ∶ 8. If the income of A is equal to the expenditure of B, then what is the ratio of savings of A and B?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of monthly incomes of A and B is 4 ∶ 5

The ratio of monthly expenditures is 3 ∶ 8

The income of A is equal to the expenditure of B

**Concept used:**

Savings = Income - Expenditure

**Calculation:**

Let the common ratio of monthly incomes & expenditures be P & Q respectively.

Now,

Monthly income of A = 4P

Monthly income of B = 5P

Now,

Monthly expenditures of A = 3Q

Monthly expenditures of B = 8Q

According to the question,

4P = 8Q

⇒ P = 2Q

Now,

Monthly income of A = 4 × 2Q = 8Q

Monthly income of B = 5 × 2Q = 10Q

Now,

Monthly savings of A = (8Q - 3Q) = 5Q

Monthly savings of B = (10Q - 8Q) = 2Q

Ratio of the savings of A & B = 5Q : 2Q = 5 : 2

**∴ The ratio of the savings of A & B is 5 : 2.**

questions.question: Two circles of radii 18 cm and 16 cm intersect each other and the length of their common chord is 20 cm. What is the distance (in cm) between their centres?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radius of the bigger circle = 18 cm

The radius of the smaller circle = 16 cm

Length of the common chord = 20 cm

**Concept used:**

If two circles intersect in two points, prove that the line through their centers is a perpendicular bisector of the common chord.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70896a65dda20e74b38267921b58313972f7e1d573dae8472a4678a702a4b98b.png] 

Here,

AB is the common chord and C1C2 is the distance between the centres of the circles.

AB is being perpendicularly bisected at point D by C₁C₂.

ΔAC₁D & ΔAC₂​D are right-angled triangles.

AC1 = 18 cm

AC2 = 16 cm

AB = 20 cm

AD = 20/2 = 10 cm

From ΔAC1D,

(AC₁)² = (C1​D)² + (AD)²

⇒ 18² = (C1​D)2 + 10²

⇒ (C1​D)2 = 324 - 100

⇒ (C1​D)2 = 224

⇒ (C1​D)2 = 14 × 16

⇒ C₁D = 4√14

From ΔAC2D,

(AC2)2 = (C2​D)2 + (AD)2

⇒ 162 = (C2​D)2 + 102

⇒ (C2​D)2 = 256 - 100

⇒ (C2​D)2 = 156

⇒ (C2​D)2 = 4 × 39

⇒ C2​D = 2√39

Now, the distance two centres of the intersecting circles = C1C2 = C1D + C2​D = (4√14 + 2√39) cm

**∴ The distance between their centres is (4√14 + 2√39) cm.**

questions.question: The volume of a wall whose height is 10 times its width and whose length is 8 times its height, is 51.2 m³ . What is the cost (in Rs.) of painting the wall on one side at the rate of Rs. 100/m²?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The volume of the wall is 51.2m³

Height = 10 × Width

Length = 8 × Height

**Concept used:**

Volume = Length × Width × Height

Surface area of one side of a wall = Height × Length

Cost of painting = Painting Cost per m² × Surface area

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7bccd8efb4bb91cce22c2c10f1d29976f56f9bebc28ac5594c4d6cefebac3b61.png] 

Let the width of the wall = A meter

Now,

the measure of height = 10 × A = 10A meter

the measure of length = 8 × 10A = 80A meter

Now,

The volume of the wall = A × 10A × 80A = 800A³ m³

According to the question,

800A3​ = 51.2

⇒ 8000 × A³ = 512

⇒ 8000 × A3 = 8 × 64

⇒ 1000 × A3 = 64

⇒ 10 × A = 4

⇒ A = 0.4

Now, 

The width of the wall = 0.4m

The height of the wall = (0.4 × 10) = 4m

The length of the wall = (4 × 8) = 32m

Now, the surface area of one side of the wall

⇒ (4 × 32) m²

= 128 m²

Now,

The cost of painting the wall on one side

⇒ Rs. (128 × 100)

⇒ Rs. 12800

**∴ The cost of painting the wall on one side at the rate of Rs. 100/m2 is Rs. 12800.**

questions.question: A boat can go 5 km upstream and 7(1)/(2) km downstream in 45 minutes. It can also go 5 km downstream and 2.5 km Upstream in 25 minutes. How much time (in minutes) will it take to go 6 km downstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The boat takes 45 mins to go 5 km upstream and 7.5 km downstream.

The boat takes 25 mins to go 5 km downstream and 2.5 km upstream

**Concept used:**

When going downstream, the speed of the boat and the flow of the river are added to calculate the net speed.

When going upstream, we take the difference between the speed of the boat and the flow of the river as the net speed. 

Distance = Time × Speed

Elimination method for solving linear equations

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the boat and the flow of the riven be B & R respectively. (in Kilometer per hours i.e. kmph)

Now,

Upstream speed = B - R = 1/P (suppose)

Downstream speed = B + R = 1/Q (suppose)

45 mins = 3/4 hour

25 mins = 5/12 hour

According to the question,

5/(B - R) + 7.5/(B + R) = 3/4

⇒ 5P + 7.5Q = 3/4 ....(1)

According to the question,

2.5/(B - R) + 5/(B + R) = 5/12

⇒ 2.5P + 5Q = 5/12 ....(2)

Solving (1) & (2) we get,

Q = 1/30 i.e. 1/(B + R) = 30

Now,

B + R = 30

The net speed during downstream = 30kmph

Now,

Time taken to cover 6km downstream

⇒ 6/30 hour

⇒ 1/5 hour

⇒ 1/5 × 60 mins

⇒ 12 mins

**∴ 12 mins will it take to go 6 km downstream.**

questions.question: The interest (in Rs.) to be paid on a sum of Rs. 30000 at 15% p,a. after 2(2)/(3) years if interest compounded yearly, is:

Rate = 15% per annum

C.I = A - P

Interest rate for first 2 years = 15%

questions.question: The average monthly salary of 60 employees of a fact Rs. 29900. If two officers are getting Rs. 90000 each and the average salary of 8 supervisors is Rs. 65000. then what is the average salary (in Rs.) of the remaining employees?

The average monthly salary of 60 employees of a factory is Rs. 29900

Total = Number of entities × Average

Calculation:

The total salary of 60 employees = Rs.(29900 × 60)

The total salary of two officers = Rs. (90000 × 2)

⇒ Rs. 180000

The total salary of 8 supervisors

⇒ Rs. (65000 × 8)

⇒ Rs. 520000

The total salary of the remaining employees

⇒ Rs. (1794000 - 180000 - 520000)

⇒ Rs. 1094000

Number of remaining employees

⇒ 60 - 2 - 8

⇒ 50

The average salary of the remaining employees

⇒ Rs. (1094000 ÷ 50)

⇒ Rs. 21880

**∴ The average salary of the remaining employees is Rs. 21880. **

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e1251b4350e51d1697a1dc5f0fa7c5c5cd591854f59cc30ede9ee3adcc6751a7.png] 

In any right angled triange like above 

a = √(b² + c² - d²)

In the question, we have b = 11, c = 8 and d = 13

So, a = √(112 + 82 - 132) 

⇒ a = √16 = 4 cm

**∴ PQ = 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

ΔABC is a right-angled triangle at ∠B.

AQ = 11cm

PC = 8cm

AC = 13cm

Concept used: 

Pythagorean theorem states that the sum of the squares on the other two sides of a right-angled triangle is equal to the square on the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle)

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d838dfc74f1cb42b530d42e7c7408ed09aba48586f3fa17365d0dac403ff27d4.png] 

Let the length of AB, BC, BQ & PB be T, S, x & y respectively.

Now,

ΔABC, ΔABQ, ΔBPC and ΔPBQ are all right-angled triangles. 

From ΔABC,

⇒ S² + T² = 13² ....(1)

From ΔABQ,

⇒ x² + T2 = 112 ....(2)

From ΔBPC,

⇒ y² + S2 = 82 ....(3)

From ΔPBQ,

⇒ x2 + y2 = PQ2 ....(4)

Adding (2) & (3),

x2 + T2 + y2 + S2 = 112 + 82

⇒ x2 + y2 + (S2 + T2) = 185

⇒ x2 + y2 = 185 - (S2 + T2) 

⇒ x2 + y2 = 185 - 169

⇒ x2 + y2 = 16

⇒ x2 + y2 = 4²

⇒ PQ² = 4² (From 4)

⇒ PQ = 4 (∵ Negative value can't be consider for length)

**∴ The length of PQ is 4cm.**
